Local patch in `src/db/types/entry.rs`:
- Rebuild attachment/custom-icon reverse references when a history version is added.
- Removing an attachment reference only removes that entry version, preserving history references.

The core creates a history checkpoint before replacing/removing attachment data.
Regression coverage: `attachment_versions_survive_replace_and_delete` in the core integration tests.
`src/db/otp.rs` uses the standard otpauth default of six digits when omitted.
Reference: https://github.com/google/google-authenticator/wiki/Key-Uri-Format
Compatibility guards in `config.rs` and `format/kdbx4/parse.rs` reject unsupported
KDF dictionary keys and nonempty outer-header comments, which upstream silently
drops. Existing ciphers and KDF implementations are reused.

Review fixes in the existing parsers and reference handling:
- Authenticate KDBX 3.1 HeaderHash before unprotecting fields; reject a missing,
  malformed or mismatched hash and invalid UTF-8 in protected text.
- Check fixed-width numeric header/dictionary values before decoding them.
- Preserve XML binary IDs, reject duplicate/dangling references, and reconstruct
  ownership for current and historical entries. Map binary IDs to emitted KDBX4
  header positions when writing, including historical references.
- Replace/remove attachment names individually when they share a binary; visit
  each binary once during deletion and remove historical ownership as well.
- Use ordinary group removal cleanup for tracked deletion while retaining its
  tombstone, so custom icons and Meta UUID references remain consistent.
Regression coverage: `review_safety.rs` and `review_attachments.rs`.

`Database::save_and_reopen` reuses the freshly derived KDF output for validation
of bytes generated within that same call. It retains the existing authenticated
decoder and fresh salts/IVs; it does not expose a caller-supplied derived key or
retain that key after validation. The temporary key is held in a `Zeroizing` buffer.
The core still compares the complete reopened model before writing the file.
Independent password/key-file reopen and KeePassXC interop tests cover this path.

`PreparedKdbx4Save` moves the library's existing KDF calculation ahead of saving.
It owns a freshly generated salt, KDF configuration and zeroizing derived-key
buffer. It has no Clone/Serialize/Debug implementation and is consumed by saving;
KDF configuration mismatches are rejected before any bytes are written. The core
holds at most one preparation per unlocked session. Master seed, IV and inner
stream key are still regenerated by the existing writer for every save.

`Database::decrypt` exposes an opaque `DecryptedKdbx` payload so the core can run
its compatibility checks on XML and then parse without a second decryption/KDF.
The XML buffer is zeroizing; existing format parsers and ciphers are reused.

`serialize_without_attachments` is a metadata-only projection for round-trip
validation. It exhaustively destructures Database so additions require updating
the projection. Attachment bytes and protection flags are checked separately by
the core, avoiding a temporary JSON array for every binary byte.

`DatabaseKey::get_key_elements` exports the existing normalized credential
components, and `from_key_elements` imports validated 32-byte components for
session Quick Unlock. Imported elements use the same existing KDBX key composition,
KDF and writer; this does not expose a caller-supplied post-KDF key. The new field
is zeroized on drop and cleared when credentials are replaced. The core's versioned
material accepts one or two components (password and/or key file), treats them as
secrets, and never persists them outside the normal encrypted KDBX. Regression
coverage: `session_key_material_*` in `lifecycle.rs`, plus Swift Quick Unlock tests.
